subject: Proposal: Scale Dedicated Pool to 2x GPUs with New Monthly Commit
messages:
From: Sara Lin <sara@acme-retail.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 09:18:42 -0800
Subject: Renewal + capacity expansion questions

Hi Rachel,

We're coming up on our Redwood Dedicated renewal and we're evaluating an increase in committed capacity. Current pool: 8 GPUs. We're interested in doubling to 16 GPUs and need a clearer picture on monthly commit mechanics and throughput guarantees. A few quick questions: 

- Can the new 16-GPU pool be phased in (8 live, then additional 8 on activation date)?
- What are the latency and throughput SLOs you can guarantee for the 16-GPU commit vs. our current profile?
- How does billing work during a phased activation?

Procurement is cc'd on this thread (procurement@acme-retail.com). Happy to set a time for a 30-min working call if helpful.

Thanks,
Sara
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Retail
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara@acme-retail.com>, procurement@acme-retail.com
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 10:03:10 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Renewal + capacity expansion questions

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Acme's ask. They're explicit about wanting to double to 16 GPUs at renewal and want options for a phased activation and clear commit/billing behavior.

High level thoughts:
- Commercial can offer a staged activation window (60 days) where only 8 GPUs bill until activation; on activation date the full monthly commit starts.
- We should pace the throughput SLA language: offer per-GPU throughput baseline + burst allowances for a short window to preserve SLOs.

Can you draft a proposal (pricing + MAP) and an ops runbook for activation? Aim to include: activation timeline, expected token/sec per allocated GPU baseline, rollback/fallback policy, and a billing example for a phased month.

Thanks — I'll book a working call with Sara and procurement for next week.

-Rachel
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara@acme-retail.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-retail.com
Date: Fri, 13 Jan 2028 08:47:22 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: Scale Dedicated Pool to 2x GPUs with New Monthly Commit

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear brief.

Attached is a commercial sketch for DL-4832: 16-GPU reserved pool with a 12-month term and a new monthly commit. Key bullets:
- Monthly commit: equivalent of 14 GPU-hours/day (committed units expressed as guaranteed slots); invoiced monthly.
- Activation flexibility: 60-day staged activation. First 30 days bill at 8-GPU rate, then a transition period where billing ramps to full commit over the next 30 days, or you can choose an immediate activation date to start the full commit.
- Price: effective blended unit price ~10% discount vs current per-GPU retail for committed 12-month term; additional volume discounts at contract signature > $X/month.

I've put an example billing scenario on page 3 of the attached PDF and a draft amendment (commit_amendment_v1.docx) for legal redlines.

Next step: can we run a 30-min working call Monday Jan 16, 9:00am PT to lock the activation approach?

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: commit_amendment_v1.docx (DOCX, 56KB)]
From: Sara Lin <sara@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-retail.com
Date: Mon, 16 Jan 2028 11:02:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: Scale Dedicated Pool to 2x GPUs with New Monthly Commit

Marissa / Rachel — thank you. A few constraints from procurement and infra: 

- Procurement prefers the billing to reflect actual activation (i.e., don't bill full commit until activation date). A 60-day staged window is fine, but billing must be capped to the active 8 GPUs until activation.
- Infra would like a guaranteed baseline throughput per-GPU (token/sec) and an SLA credit table if we see sustained degradation > 10% for more than 10 minutes.
- We need a short ops runbook for activation and fallback in case we hit performance regressions. Our target go-live is end of February, ideally Feb 28.

I'll join the Monday call.

—Sara
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara@acme-retail.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Jan 2028 09:36:14 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: Scale Dedicated Pool to 2x GPUs with New Monthly Commit

Sara — quick technical notes and a draft activation runbook attached. Highlights: 

- Throughput baseline: we can guarantee a steady-state of 1.2M tokens/min per GPU for your current model mix (based on recent profiling). This is the baseline tied to the commit. 
- Burst allowance: up to 1.7M tokens/min per GPU for 5-minute windows; sustained bursts will be serviced subject to capacity and may incur throttling if platform contention occurs.
- SLA credit: propose credits equivalent to 5% of monthly commit for each hour of sustained degradation beyond the threshold, capped at 50% for the month (commercial to confirm).
- Activation runbook: attached ops_activation_runbook.pdf — includes canary activation (10% traffic), KV cache warm-up guidance, rollback steps, and a smoke-test checklist.

I'll update the runbook with any procurement/legal inputs after the call.

-Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ops_activation_runbook.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]

Thanks everyone — good progress. Recap and agreed next steps for DL-4832: 

1) Commercial: Marissa to finalize amendment with the phased activation billing language (bill at 8 GPUs until activation date; optional ramp schedule if Acme requests). Marissa to include the SLA credit table and pricing appendix.
2) Ops: Karthik to finalize the activation runbook and a 48-hour canary plan; include the KV warming steps and rollback commands.
3) Legal/Procurement: Acme to review the amendment; proposed signature target Jan 28 to allow Feb 28 activation.
4) MAP call: Rachel to schedule 30-min sync Jan 23, 9:00am PT — primary goal: confirm activation date and DocuSign next steps.

Sara — once you confirm procurement's redlines we'll prep the DocuSign packet and send the amendment for signature.

Best,
